titles.title: UnrealGold
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: Unreal Gold 226b (System\Manifest.ini Version=226b; Unreal plus Return to Na Pali/UPak). The game renderer is D3DDrv 226b (System\D3DDrv.dll, md5 f924e209e7bc23b90b6f0360174683d3). The menus are UWindow/UMenu, reached through Console=UPak.UPakConsole, then UMenu.UnrealConsole, then UWindow.WindowConsole.
titles.launch_sets: On the four 1080p LCD boxes the game starts fullscreen at 1920x1080x32. How it gets there: 'Play Unreal Gold.bat' calls FLEETRES.BAT, then FLEETRES.EXE -ini writes [WinDrv.WindowsClient] FullscreenViewportX/Y=%FR_W%/%FR_H% (1920/1080 when the EDID says LCD) and StartupFullscreen=True into System\Unreal.ini. It also sets GameRenderDevice, WindowedRenderDevice and RenderDevice to %FR_UE1DEV%, which is D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice (GlideDrv only when GlideRender=1, and no LCD box has that). gameres.h has the same three INI rules, so GAMESYNC writes the same values at sync time. The staged Unreal.ini itself still says 1024x768, but that is overwritten on each box. The mechanism is present and current: stage-fleetres.py --check reports 213 launchers current, and the only failure is Thief2. FLEETRES.EXE (md5 bb180f3b…) is identical to the repo's provisioning/fleetres/FLEETRES.EXE, and FLEETRES.BAT (md5 23edd351…) is identical across all five titles. D3DDrv's SetRes best-match searches the full DirectDraw list (the fields at object 0x954), not the capped GetRes list, so starting at 1080p works even where the menu cannot list it. The compat DB and the 2026-08-31 captures show 1920x1080 frames on .123, .240 and .246 (now .195). .145 has never been tested.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver but is cut short. Esc opens the UWindow desktop (UMenu.UMenuRootWindow); the path is Options > Preferences > Video > Resolution. UMenuVideoClientWindow.LoadAvailableSettings fills a combo that cannot be typed into (SetEditable False), copying ConsoleCommand("GetRes") word for word. D3DDrv answers GetRes, and in that handler it keeps only 16-bpp DirectDraw modes (cmp [desc+0x54],0x10), removes duplicates, does NOT sort, and prints at most 16 entries (100064f5: cmp edi,0x10 / jge). The only other filter is a max-mode clamp that defaults to 0x7fffffff and is lowered only for 3dfx Voodoo 1/2. 1920x1080 is the largest mode, so it is last in the ascending list. Tonight's GAMERES mode counts: .123 has 15 modes, so 1920x1080 is entry 15 and is listed. .145 has 16, so it is entry 16 and is listed with no margin. .195 has 20 and .240 has 24 (29 in another state), so it is dropped. The predicted menu tops out at 1440x900 on .195 and 1280x768 on .240. This assumes DirectDraw lists the same 16-bpp set in the same ascending order as GDI; that is not yet proven on the boxes. The classic UnrealShare.UnrealVideoMenu (var string Resolutions[16]) is not reachable from Esc.
titles.evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ue-survey/01-unrealgold-226b-D3DDrv-GetRes.asm.txt (GetRes, EnumModesCallback and EnumDisplayModes disassembly; the cap is at file offset 0x64f5, bytes 83 ff 10); 05-unrealgold-menu-scripts.txt (the UMenu video page script, the WindowConsole Esc to LaunchUWindow chain, and the classic Resolutions[16] menu); 09-lcd-mode-lists-and-predicted-menus.json (per-box mode lists from tonight's GAMERES captures, with the predicted menus); 10-unreal-226final-patch-D3DDrv.txt (the D3DDrv carved from the share's unreal-patch-226-final.exe has the identical capped code); 11-stage-fleetres-check.txt; 12-compat-db-render-rows-lcd-boxes.json; prior-2026-08-31-contact-sheet.png. The decoded WindowConsole ConsoleKey default is 192 (tilde). The staged User.ini binds F9=Shot and F11=Shot. The Unreal.ini sections [UMenu.UnrealConsole] RootWindow=UMenu.UMenuRootWindow and UWindowKey=IK_Esc.
titles.fix: Lift D3DDrv's 16-entry cap with a one-byte edit of System\D3DDrv.dll: at file offset 0x64f5, change 83 FF 10 (cmp edi,16) to 83 FF 7F. The UMenu combo has no limit of its own, so every 16-bpp mode, including 1920x1080, then appears. The order stays DirectDraw's, which is ascending in practice. GameRenderDevice stays D3DDrv, as README-FLEET requires. I do not recommend the alternatives: (a) switching the renderer to the 226 OpenGlDrv (its GetRes is uncapped) contradicts the D3DDrv decision in README-FLEET, and the launcher's FR_UE1DEV lines would overwrite an ini-only change anyway; (b) OldUnreal 227k.
titles.fix_source: No payload is needed: it is a one-byte edit of the staged file, with the original backed up under Games-Library\_patches. The official 226 Final patch on the share (Game Updates/unreal-patch-226-final.exe, not applied) ships a D3DDrv with the same cap, so it does not help. OldUnreal 227k would have to be downloaded from oldunreal.com. It is work-in-progress and SSE2-only, which rules out .124, .133 and .143, and it cannot interoperate with the fleet's 226 LAN hosting.
titles.fix_risk: Low for play and multiplayer. D3DDrv.dll is a native renderer, not a network package, and 226 has no anti-cheat. GetRes builds its output in a string device that grows as needed, and UMenu parses any number of entries. Remaining risks: this edits a vendor binary, so record the md5 before and after. The edit keeps the file size, so publish it through gvfs rather than smbclient: smbclient stamps an Oct 2007 mtime, and GAMESYNC would skip a same-size file. Then verify the byte on a box. Prove the fix on .195 and .240, the boxes where the cap bites.
titles.hw_check: Start the game the way the shortcut does: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\UnrealGold" "Play Unreal Gold.bat" (the bat also deletes Running.ini). The UWindow menu moves its cursor by relative mouse deltas, so the agent's UICLICK cannot drive it. The console is keyboard-driven, though, and GetRes typed there returns the same string the Video combo is filled with. Steps: UIKEY TILDE (ConsoleKey 192 opens the UWindow console), UIKEY TEXT:getres, UIKEY ENTER, then UIKEY TEXT:getcurrentres and UIKEY ENTER. To capture: use SCREENSHOT 0, since GDI captured Unreal Gold on .123, .240 and .246. Where GDI returns black, press F9/F11 (Shot) and DOWNLOAD System\Shot####.bmp. To pass, the getres output must contain 1920x1080 on .123, .145, .195 and .240. Expected today: present on .123 and .145, absent on .195 and .240. For the actual drop-down (Options > Preferences > Video > Resolution), a person has to open it once. Clean up with taskkill /f /im "Unreal.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: The numbers for .195 and .240 are predictions from the code and the GDI mode lists. They depend on DirectDraw exposing the same ascending 16-bpp set, and the on-box getres check settles that. The .145 result has no margin (exactly 16 modes). .240's EDID flapped tonight (none at 23:40, present at 23:55); without an EDID, FLEETRES treats the monitor as a CRT and the game starts at the persisted desktop mode, not 1080p. Other agents are running Quake III tests on these boxes right now, so coordinate before launching games. PER-TITLE-STATUS.md's "1080p" entry describes launch only, not the menu.

titles.title: UnrealTournament
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: UT99 OldUnreal 469e ([FirstRun] 469, install.reg Version 469, the Engine.dll and Core.dll strings reference 469e; Manifest.ini still says 436). GameRenderDevice=D3D9Drv.D3D9RenderDevice, 469e's own Direct3D 9 renderer. It needs SSE2 and its PEs are XP-only.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32 fullscreen on the LCD boxes, by the same FLEETRES mechanism: 'Play Unreal Tournament.bat' writes [WinDrv.WindowsClient] FullscreenViewportX/Y=%FR_W%/%FR_H% and StartupFullscreen=True into System\UnrealTournament.ini. gameres.h has the matching rules, and stage-fleetres --check reports it current. Verified in the compat DB: .123 is 'd3d 1920x1080', and on .246 (now .195) '469e renders FULLSCREEN at native 1920x1080 via D3D9Drv'. The .240 capture is a 1920x1080 frame. .145 has never been tested.
titles.menu_source: The full list, taken from the driver. The path is Options > Preferences > Video > Resolution. It uses the same UMenuVideoClientWindow code as Unreal Gold (verbatim GetRes, not editable). D3D9Drv's GetRes keeps every mode whose depth equals the viewport's ColorBytes*8 (32 here). It skips only 320x200 and 640x400, removes duplicates, sorts with appQsort, and prints every entry with no cap. The same array and the same depth filter feed the fullscreen SetRes best-match, and that reached 1920x1080 on .123 and .246, so the array contains 1920x1080x32 there. The windowed/borderless path goes through 469e's WinDrv, which uses a built-in 54-entry table (320x240 … 1920x1080 … 15360x8640) clipped to the desktop, and that table includes 1920x1080 as well.
titles.evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ue-survey/04-ut469e-D3D9Drv-GetRes.asm.txt (GetRes disassembly, the skip constants decoded as 320,200,640,400, the SetRes best-match over obj+0x18f0c, and the WinDrv windowed table); 06-ut469e-ut436-UMenu-video.txt; 12-compat-db-render-rows-lcd-boxes.json; the 1920x1080 frames /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/perbox/evidence/123_UnrealTournament_Play_Unreal_Tournament.png and 246_UnrealTournament_Play_Unreal_Tournament.png. The UnrealTournament.ini [D3D9Drv.D3D9RenderDevice] section is staged, with UseDirectInput=False and ConsoleKey=192.
titles.fix_source: n/a - already in the tree (OldUnreal 469e D3D9Drv)
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\UnrealTournament" "Play Unreal Tournament.bat". The UWindow menu cursor is relative-mouse and cannot be driven by UICLICK, so use the keyboard console: UIKEY TILDE, UIKEY TEXT:getres, UIKEY ENTER. The expected output is a sorted list ending in or containing 1920x1080, with getcurrentres returning 1920x1080. Capture with SCREENSHOT 0, since GDI captured 469e D3D9 fullscreen on .246 and .123, or fall back to F11 (Shot) and System\Shot####.bmp. A person can confirm the drop-down under Options > Preferences > Video. Close with taskkill /f /im "UnrealTournament.exe"; the Play bat clears Running.ini on the next start.
titles.verifier_notes: If a player uses the video-driver button to switch to 469e's own D3DDrv.dll, that renderer also filters to 16-bpp in GetRes (I did not check it for the 16-entry cap). It is not the staged renderer.

titles.title: UnrealTournament436
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: UT99 retail 436 ([FirstRun] 436). GameRenderDevice=OpenGLDrv.OpenGLRenderDevice (retail 436 OpenGlDrv.dll, md5 12031672…) with FullscreenColorBits=16. The tree was staged for the pre-SSE2 boxes, but its requires.json excludes nothing, so it is also deployed on .123, .145, .240 and .246/.195.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 at 16 bpp, fullscreen. The FLEETRES block in both launchers ('Play Unreal Tournament 436.bat' and 'Join fleet UT99 server - 436.bat') writes FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into System\UnrealTournament.ini; gameres.h has the matching rules, and the launchers are current. Verified in the compat DB: .123 is 1920x1080 fullscreen and joined the fleet server. .246 (now .195) is 'Retail 436 verified FULLSCREEN 1920x1080' through the F11 Shot bind, while GDI was black there. .240 runs, but its GDI frame is black. .145 has never been tested.
titles.menu_source: The full list, taken from the driver. The path is Options > Preferences > Video, and the retail 436 UMenuVideoClientWindow copies GetRes verbatim into a combo that cannot be typed into. OpenGLDrv's Init fills Modes from an unfiltered EnumDisplaySettingsA(NULL,i) loop. GetRes keeps the modes whose bpp equals the viewport's ColorBytes*8 (16 here), skips 320x200 and 640x400, removes duplicates, sorts with appQsort, and prints every entry with no cap. 1920x1080x16 exists on these drivers: ChangeDisplaySettings to it succeeded on .246/.195 and on .123. Caveat: the Video page's driver button can switch this tree to its own D3DDrv.dll, and that renderer has the same 16-bpp-only, 16-entry cap as Unreal Gold (file offset 0x659f, bytes 83 ff 10).
titles.evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ue-survey/03-ut436-OpenGlDrv-GetRes.asm.txt (GetRes and the EnumDisplaySettingsA loop, plus the 436 D3DDrv cap); 06-ut469e-ut436-UMenu-video.txt; 12-compat-db-render-rows-lcd-boxes.json; the 1920x1080 frame /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/perbox/evidence/123_UnrealTournament436_Play_Unreal_Tournament_436.png. The staged UnrealTournament.ini has GameRenderDevice=OpenGLDrv, RenderDevice=GlideDrv and FullscreenColorBits=16. The staged User.ini binds F11=Shot.
titles.fix: None is needed for the staged OpenGL renderer. Optional: if players might switch this tree to Direct3D, apply the same one-byte cap lift to its D3DDrv.dll (file offset 0x659f: 83 FF 10 to 83 FF 7F).
titles.fix_source: n/a for the staged renderer (already in the tree). The optional D3DDrv edit needs no payload, only an edit of the staged file.
titles.fix_risk: None for the recommended course (no change). The optional D3DDrv edit is a native renderer DLL with no network role, but it keeps the file size, so publish it through gvfs.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\UnrealTournament436" "Play Unreal Tournament 436.bat", then UIKEY TILDE, UIKEY TEXT:getres, UIKEY ENTER. Expect a sorted list of 16-bpp modes that includes 1920x1080. On .195 (Windows 7) GDI returns black for this OpenGL surface, so press F11 (Shot) and DOWNLOAD System\Shot####.bmp; that route is proven on .246. On the XP boxes, try SCREENSHOT 0 first (.240's GDI frame was black, so use F11 there too). The UWindow drop-down itself is relative-mouse and needs a person. Close with taskkill /f /im "UnrealTournament.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: Both UT trees are deployed on the LCD boxes, and both desktop icons launch an exe named UnrealTournament.exe, so check the image path (wmic) before attributing a result to one tree.

titles.title: UT2004
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 2: UT2004 ECE build 3369 (System\Build.ini UT2004_Build_[2005-11-23_16.22]). RenderDevice=D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice (Direct3D 8). Menus are GUI2K4, with UT2K4GUIController and ExtendedConsole.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen. 'Play UT2004.bat' and 'Join fleet UT2004 server.bat' call FLEETRES, which writes [WinDrv.WindowsClient] FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into System\UT2004.ini. gameres.h has the matching rules, and the launchers are current. Verified in the compat DB at 1920x1080 on .123, .240 and .246/.195 (the .123 capture is the 1920x1080 main menu). .145 has never been tested.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table plus the current mode. The path is Settings > Display (UT2K4Tab_DetailSettings, which is PanelClass[0]). GetComboOptions seeds co_Resolution from var() DisplayMode DisplayModes[17] = 320x240 512x384 640x480 800x500 800x600 1024x640 1024x768 1152x768 1152x864 1280x800 1280x854 1280x960 1280x1024 1600x1024 1600x1200 1680x1050 1920x1200. That table has NO 1920x1080, is not config, and every combo is set ReadOnly. CheckSupportedResolutions then removes entries that D3DDrv's SUPPORTEDRESOLUTION rejects (a lookup of WxH plus depth in the D3D adapter-mode list). InternalOnLoadINI then inserts the CURRENT resolution in sorted position with AddNewResolution(Controller.GetCurrentRes()). So 1920x1080 is listed only because the fleet launcher starts the game at 1920x1080. It is not a table entry. I found no bPersistent default for the page, so the page is probably rebuilt on each open. If a player switches to another mode and reopens Settings, 1920x1080 is probably gone until the next launch. XInterface.Tab_VideoSettings (DisplayModes[23]) is never referenced by GUI2K4.
titles.evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ue-survey/08-ut2004-GUI2K4-resolution.txt (the UT2K4Tab_DetailSettings script, the GetComboOptions branch, the DisplayModes[17] defaults decoded from the class export at offset 145901, the non-config findings for MainMenuOptions/DisplayModes, the PanelClass order, and the D3DDrv SUPPORTEDRESOLUTION disassembly); 12-compat-db-render-rows-lcd-boxes.json; /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/perbox/evidence/123_UT2004_Play_UT2004.png. UT2004.ini [Engine.Engine] GUIController=GUI2K4.UT2K4GUIController (a config key). [XInterface.ExtendedConsole] ConsoleHotKey=192. UCC.exe is present in System\.
titles.fix: None is required for the launcher-started case. Optional hardening, so that 1920x1080 is always in the list: build a small client-side package, e.g. FleetGUI.u, with the tree's own System\UCC.exe in the build VM. It would contain three classes. (1) FleetTab_DetailSettings extends UT2K4Tab_DetailSettings, with defaultproperties that redefine all 17 DisplayModes in ascending order and include 1280x720, 1366x768, 1600x900 and 1920x1080. (2) FleetSettingsPage extends UT2K4SettingsPage, with PanelClass(0)="FleetGUI.FleetTab_DetailSettings". (3) FleetGUIController extends UT2K4GUIController, overriding GetSettingsPage() to return FleetGUI.FleetSettingsPage. Then set the staged UT2004.ini [Engine.Engine] GUIController=FleetGUI.FleetGUIController. No stock package is edited.
titles.fix_source: Nothing to download. The package would be built in the build VM from the staged tree, whose UCC.exe is present. It is not yet written.
titles.fix_risk: Low for fleet multiplayer: the package is client-only GUI, not a ServerPackage, and the stock GUI2K4 and XInterface GUIDs are unchanged. Moderate engineering risk: a GUIController class that fails to load breaks every menu, so prove it in the build VM and then on a box. It is unknown whether public-internet anti-cheat (UTComp/ANTI-TCC) on the favourites servers objects to a custom GUIController.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\UT2004" "Play UT2004.bat". GUI2K4 is expected to accept keyboard focus (arrows, Tab, Enter), but that is unproven on this fleet. From the main menu, arrow to 'Settings' (6th of 7 items), press ENTER, and screenshot at each step. The page opens on the Display tab, and the Resolution combo should read 1920x1080. SCREENSHOT 0 works here, since GDI captured UT2004 on .123, .240 and .246. Console alternative: UIKEY TILDE (ConsoleHotKey 192), UIKEY TEXT:getcurrentres, ENTER, then UIKEY TEXT:SUPPORTEDRESOLUTION WIDTH=1920 HEIGHT=1080 BITDEPTH=32, ENTER; expect 1920x1080 and True/1. Note the staged User.ini carries no key binds, only installer window positions. Close with taskkill /f /im "UT2004.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: The "yes" depends on the launcher: the fixed table itself lacks 1920x1080. The claim that the page is not persistent was inferred from finding no bPersistent tag in the decoded class chain. It was not observed.

titles.title: DeusEx
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: Deus Ex 1112fm (SYSTEM\MANIFEST.INI Version=1112fm). GameRenderDevice is Deus Ex's own D3DDrv (SYSTEM\D3DDRV.DLL, md5 6179c83ce1d7516908e5442ebfb4d154). The UI is Deus Ex's own (Root=DeusEx.DeusExRootWindow, extension window system).
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32 fullscreen. 'Play Deus Ex.bat' (and the headless 'Host Deus Ex Multiplayer.bat') call FLEETRES, which writes [WinDrv.WindowsClient] FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into SYSTEM\DeusEx.ini (Windows paths are case-insensitive). gameres.h has the matching rules, and the launchers are current. SetRes best-match uses the full DirectDraw list, so the game starts at 1080p even where the menu cannot list it. Verified in the compat DB at 1920x1080 on .123 and .246/.195 (1920x1080 logo frames). .240 'runs', but its GDI frame is black. .145 has never been tested.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver and is cut short twice. The path is Settings > Display > Resolution, which is MenuChoice_Resolution. Its GetScreenResolutions parses ConsoleCommand("GetRes") into enumText[40], but reads only the first 16 tokens (local string Resolutions[16]; while ResNum < ArrayCount(Resolutions), compiled as 07 4b 01 96 00 4b 5f 2c 10 16) and drops widths under 640. GetRes comes from D3DDRV.DLL, which has the same code as Unreal Gold's 226 D3DDrv: 16-bpp only, unsorted, at most 16 entries (100062ce cmp edi,0x10). Predicted: listed on .123 (15 modes) and .145 (16, no margin); missing on .195 (20) and .240 (24 or 29). There is also a trap: when the current mode is absent, LoadSetting selects entry 0, and pressing OK on the Display screen runs SaveSetting() on every choice, which issues SetRes to that entry (e.g. 640x480). The stock OpenGlDrv's GetRes is uncapped, but the menu's 16-token limit would still apply.
titles.evidence: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ue-survey/02-deusex-1112fm-D3DDRV-GetRes.asm.txt (the cap is at file offset 0x62ce, bytes 83 ff 10; the max-mode clamp is 0x7fffffff except for 3dfx); 07-deusex-menu-scripts.txt (the MenuChoice_Resolution script, enumText[40], the SaveSettings loop, and the compiled-bytecode hex showing 2c 10 at DEUSEX.U file offset 0x4607cd/0x4607ce); 09-lcd-mode-lists-and-predicted-menus.json; 12-compat-db-render-rows-lcd-boxes.json; 13-md5-of-analysed-binaries.txt (DEUSEX.U md5 d343da03a6d311ee412dfae4b52ff975). The staged USER.INI has F11=Shot, T= (empty) and Tilde= (empty). Kentie's own changelog (https://kentie.net/article/dxguide/files/Readme.htm, web source) says his resolution drop-down is Deus Exe's launcher dialog (v6+), and v6 dropped XP.
titles.fix: Two one-byte edits, neither of which changes a file size. (1) SYSTEM\D3DDRV.DLL, file offset 0x62ce: change 83 FF 10 to 83 FF 7F, so the renderer returns every 16-bpp mode. (2) SYSTEM\DEUSEX.U, file offset 0x4607ce: change 0x10 to 0x28. That byte is the IntConstByte 16 in 'JumpIfNot(resNum < 16)' inside MenuChoice_Resolution.GetScreenResolutions, and 0x28 = 40 = the size of enumText, so no out-of-bounds write is possible. Both edits are required: (1) alone does not help, because the menu still reads only 16 tokens. Kentie's Deus Exe is NOT a fix, since its resolution list lives in its own dialog and needs Vista from v6. A cleaner but larger alternative is a new client-side UnrealScript package: a DeusExRootWindow subclass selected through [Engine.Engine] Root= that substitutes a MenuScreenDisplay/MenuChoice_Resolution subclass. That needs the Deus Ex SDK's UCC, which is not in the tree and not on the share.
titles.fix_source: No payload is needed for the byte edits: edit the staged files and back up the originals under Games-Library\_patches. The SDK alternative would require downloading the Deus Ex 1112f SDK.
titles.fix_risk: Moderate. DEUSEX.U is the game's network package. The byte edit keeps its GUID and size, so the fleet's vanilla 1112fm deusex-server should still accept these clients. Whether 1112fm checks package contents is unverified, so both a join to the fleet server and a box-hosted LAN game must be proven again after the change, and every box must receive the same file through GAMESYNC. Both edits keep file sizes, so publish through gvfs (an smbclient 2007 mtime would make GAMESYNC skip the file) and verify on a box. These are edits to core vendor files: keep the md5s and backups.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\DeusEx" "Play Deus Ex.bat". The menu pointer moves by relative mouse deltas, so UICLICK misses, and the staged USER.INI binds no console key. Keyboard attempt: MenuUIScreenWindow cycles the focused choice with Left/Right. If Tab or arrow focus can reach Settings > Display > Resolution, press UIKEY RIGHT repeatedly and screenshot each value. GDI worked for Deus Ex on .123 and .246; on .240 it was black, so use F11 (Shot) there and DOWNLOAD SYSTEM\Shot####.bmp. Leave the screen with Escape (Cancel), never Enter/OK, because OK applies the shown resolution. Otherwise a person does it once. Proxy for the list: Unreal Gold's console getres on the same box returns the identical D3DDrv list (same code), and Deus Ex keeps the first 16 of those tokens that are at least 640 wide. Close with taskkill /f /im "DeusEx.exe"; the Play bat clears Running.ini on the next start.
titles.verifier_notes: As with Unreal Gold, the .195 and .240 results are code-plus-mode-list predictions, and .145 has no margin. This title was already patched once (1002f to 1112fm from kentie.net); record any further binary change in _patches/README.txt with md5s.
